The deadweight loss is the area between the demand and supply curves from the quantity with tax \(Q_t\) to the equilibrium quantity without tax \(Q_0\).  
Without tax, equilibrium occurs where demand price equals supply price. From the data, \(D(Q)-S(Q)=0\) between \(Q=1190\) and \(Q=1200\). Linear interpolation gives \(Q_0 = 1197\).  
With the tax, the condition is \(D(Q)-S(Q)=850\). This occurs between \(Q=0\) and \(Q=10\); linear interpolation gives \(Q_t = \frac{10}{7}\).  

The deadweight loss is  
\[
\int_{Q_t}^{Q_0} (D(Q)-S(Q))\,dQ = \int_{0}^{Q_0} f(Q)\,dQ - \int_{0}^{Q_t} f(Q)\,dQ,
\]  
where \(f(Q)=D(Q)-S(Q)\).  

The integral from \(0\) to \(Q_0\) is the sum of trapezoidal areas on \([0,1190]\) plus the triangular area on \([1190,1197]\):  
\[
\int_{0}^{1190} f = 4290 + 10\sum_{i=1}^{118} f_i = 501710,\qquad
\int_{1190}^{1197} f = \frac{1}{2}\cdot7\cdot7 = \frac{49}{2},
\]  
so \(\int_0^{Q_0} f = 501710 + \frac{49}{2} = \frac{1003469}{2}\).  

The integral from \(0\) to \(Q_t\) is the area of a trapezoid:  
\[
\int_0^{10/7} f = \frac{851+850}{2}\cdot\frac{10}{7} = 1215 = \frac{2430}{2}.
\]  

Thus  
\[
\text{DWL} = \frac{1003469}{2} - \frac{2430}{2} = \frac{1001039}{2}.
\]  

This fraction is already reduced.

ANSWER: 1001039/2
